newsitem.title: USA: Rains set to slow harvesting in eastern Corn Belt.
newsitem.headline: Rains set to slow harvesting in eastern Corn Belt.

text.p: Rains look set to sweep across the eastern Corn Belt late Wednesday and into Thursday, slowing harvest progress although conditions should remain largely dry further west, meteorologists said.

"We are looking for 0.50 to 2.00 inches of rain tonight and tomorrow in Ohio, Indiana, most of Illinois and a good chunk of Missouri," said Mike Palmerino, senior agricultural meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
"That certainly is going to slow down this harvest in those states for the next few days," he added.
Weekly state crop reports, issued earlier this week, indicated harvest progress was already running well behind normal in the eastern Corn Belt.
Indiana corn harvest was 47 percent complete as of Sunday, behind the average pace of 72 percent, with Ohio 37 percent done, versus a normal 63 percent.
Palmerino also noted that cloud cover would slow drying out of fields in Ohio and Michigan although weather should start to improve late Sunday.
More favorable drying conditions were expected in Illinois and harvest may resume fairly quickly in the north, he said.

"In Illinois, especially northern Illinois, they will be able to get back into the fields as early as Saturday," Palmerino said, noting rain should total only about 0.50 inches in the north but nearer 2.00 inches in the south.
Further west in Minnesota, Iowa and Nebraska, scattered showers of 0.10 to 0.50 inches are expected Wednesday but should be followed by prolonged dry weather, he said.

"There is a long period of dry weather coming up for the western Corn Belt, starting on Thursday and continuing for the first part of next week. It may be enough to allow much of this harvest to finish up," he said.

Iowa's corn harvest was 62 percent complete, as of Sunday, slightly behind the normal 71 percent with Nebraska 71 percent done, marginally above the average pace of 70 percent, according to weekly state crop updates.
Jon Davis, meteorologist with Smith Barney, said skies should clear in the western Corn Belt late Wednesday and the eastern belt by late Thursday.

"The rains the next few days will cause some minor disruptions in fieldwork operations. The extended stretch of dry weather thereafter will allow late harvest activity to resume," Davis wrote in his daily weather outlook update.
